instruction: Select all images containing a duck.

game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary ducks count, and so do the duck reading a newspaper on a bench and the duck standing on wheels: impossible, but still ducks. The robot duck and the wooden decoy are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The swan, the penguin and the pigeon are not ducks.

correct: Ducks identified. They have been told to carry on.
Correct. All ducks are in a row.
partial: Partially correct. A duck has slipped away unnoticed.
Partially correct. Your duck count is under review.
incorrect: Incorrect. The Department will not be ruffled by this.

selection_review.reason: Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary ducks (white Pekin duck on a lawn, three-quarter view; mandarin drake swimming, side view), two impossible ducks (generated mallard on a park bench holding a newspaper in human hands; generated female mallard standing on small wheels), two borderline objects shaped like ducks (generated metal robot duck on a lake shore; generated carved wooden decoy floating on a lake) and three non-member birds (mute swan, gentoo penguin, feral pigeon). Water and white plumage appear among targets, borderline cases and non-members alike, so neither decides. Views, colours and settings vary within each role. The mallard drake, the walking mandarin, the rubber duck, the three-headed duck and the earlier renders remain in the collection for later versions.
